about: Star Wars Yoda is a close-up of the Jedi Master Yoda as a puppet from the original trilogy: wrinkled green skin, long pointed ears, a ragged robe and a calm, slightly amused half-smile while he clasps his walking stick. He looks like a wise teacher about to deliver a lesson you won't like. The meme uses that patient expression to dispense advice, gentle scolding or obvious truths in his famous backwards word order, where the object comes first and the verb comes last. Turning everyday nagging into Yoda-speak makes even mundane instructions sound like ancient Jedi wisdom.
origin: Yoda first appeared in The Empire Strikes Back in 1980, played and voiced by puppeteer Frank Oz. His inverted sentence structure has been parodied ever since.
usage:
Use the top box to start the sentence and the bottom box to finish it, and write it in Yoda's inverted grammar: "fix the bug, you must" / "before friday". The fun is in forcing modern, nerdy or petty advice into that ancient-master cadence.

Good targets are advice everyone ignores (sleep, backups, stretching), study tips, gym wisdom and gaming lessons. Ending with "hmm" or "yes" adds to the voice. Keep both lines short; Yoda never rambles.
ideas: back up your files, you will
read the syllabus, you did not
skip leg day, you must not
